description:
## Outcome

Two independent readiness reviews decide whether to create follow-up publication tasks for Winget and `homebrew/core`.

## Work

1. Evaluate Winget after Windows signing and service operations are stable. Review manifest, installer, identity, update, and support requirements.
2. Evaluate `homebrew/core` after stable repeatable releases, Linux support, tap history, and sufficient project use exist.
3. Record objective evidence, unmet criteria, owner, maintenance cost, and security requirements for each channel.
4. If a channel is ready, create one separate implementation task with its own acceptance tests.
5. If it is not ready, record the next review trigger and do not submit a weak package.
6. Keep MSI and other installer options separate from the ZIP and Scoop contract.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Winget and `homebrew/core` each have a clear independent decision.
- [ ] Decisions cite current channel requirements and project evidence.
- [ ] A positive decision creates a bounded follow-up issue.
- [ ] A negative decision states measurable review triggers.
- [ ] No channel submission occurs through an undocumented manual path.
- [ ] Windows ARM64 remains a later target unless a separate plan approves it.

## Tests

Validate decision templates and any created follow-up issue dependencies. Channel implementation tests belong to those follow-up tasks.

## Non-goals

Do not submit to Winget or `homebrew/core` only to close this review task.
title: Evaluate Winget and homebrew-core readiness
